say: Shout their name. Shake their shoulders.
steps.quote: Check for signs of an opioid overdose. Slow, weak or no breathing / Falling asleep or can't wake up / Gurgling sounds in throat / Very small pupils / Cold, clammy skin / Discolored skin (especially lips and fingernails)

steps.sub: Slow, gurgling, or gasping is not normal.
steps.quote: A first aid provider who encounters a person with suspected opioid overdose who is unresponsive and not breathing or not breathing normally should activate the emergency response system, provide high-quality CPR (compressions plus ventilation), and administer naloxone.

say: Do you have Narcan? Naloxone spray?
steps.quote: An opioid antagonist (e.g., naloxone) should be given to people with respiratory arrest from suspected opioid overdose. Trained rescuers, lay rescuers, and members of the general public can all administer naloxone.

steps.sub: Head back. Push the plunger firmly.
say: Lay them on their back. Tilt the head back.
Tip in one nostril. Push the plunger firmly.
steps.quote: Lay the person on their back. Tilt their head back. [...] Do NOT test spray the Narcan. They need the full dose. Put the tip of the nozzle in 1 nostril. Push the plunger firmly to give the entire dose.

A first aid provider who encounters a person with suspected opioid overdose who is unresponsive and not breathing or not breathing normally should activate the emergency response system, provide high-quality CPR (compressions plus ventilation), and administer naloxone.

steps.sub: Watch. Second dose if no change.
say: Roll them onto their side. Top knee bent.
Watch for two to three minutes.
doneSay: Still not waking up? Give a second dose.
steps.quote: Roll the person on their side. Bend their top knee to keep them from rolling on their stomach. [...] Watch to see if they wake up or start breathing normally. If they don't within 2-3 minutes, give a 2nd dose in the other nostril.

say: Use a new spray, in the other nostril.
steps.quote: You will need a new nasal spray for the 2nd dose.

say: No naloxone. Is the breathing normal?
steps.quote: A first aid provider who encounters a person with suspected opioid overdose who is unresponsive and not breathing or not breathing normally should activate the emergency response system, provide high-quality CPR (compressions plus ventilation), and administer naloxone.

steps.sub: It can wear off. Wait for EMS.
say: Stay with them until help arrives.
If they get sleepy again, tell me.
steps.quote: If they still don't respond and you have more Narcan, you can keep giving new doses every 2-3 minutes in a different nostril each time. Do this until they wake up or emergency help arrives.
steps.note: "It can wear off" is a common teaching point not stated in this source; reviewer to confirm or remove.
